sections.title: Functional Grammar: Different Parts of Speech for the Same Word
sections.content: Step 1: Look at the word's role, not its form. Step 2: Is it the Subject, Object, Modifier, or Main Verb in the sentence? Step 3: If it is used as a name, it's a Noun; if it describes an action, it's an Adverb; if it describes a Noun, it's an Adjective; if it is the action itself, it's a Verb. Step 4: Changing the syntax (word order) can change the Part of Speech. Step 5: Example — He kept the fast. (fast = Noun), He ran fast. (fast = Adverb), He is a fast runner. (fast = Adjective), They fast on Mondays. (fast = Verb).

sections.title: Gerund vs Present Participle (V1+ing)
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the V1+ing form (running, swimming). Step 2: Check if it is acting like a Noun or an Adjective. Step 3: If it is a Subject/Object → Gerund (Swimming is good). Step 4: If it is describing a Noun → Present Participle (a swimming boy). Step 5: A Gerund can be replaced by the pronoun 'it'; a participle cannot.

sections.title: Various Functions of the Infinitive (to + V1)
sections.content: Step 1: Identify 'to + base verb' (to read, to play). Step 2: If it acts as a Subject/Object → Noun (To read is useful). Step 3: If it qualifies a Noun → Adjective (I have a book to read). Step 4: If it states a purpose/reason → Adverb (He came to study). Step 5: Determine its role based on its position and meaning.

sections.title: Inversion with Negative/Restrictive Adverbs
sections.content: Step 1: Look for a negative or restrictive adverb at the beginning of the sentence (Hardly, Never, Rarely, Seldom, No sooner). Step 2: If a sentence starts with such an adverb, subject-auxiliary inversion will occur. Step 3: The auxiliary verb will come before the subject. Step 4: Use 'than' and 'when' correctly with Hardly/No sooner. Step 5: Example — Hardly had I reached when it started raining. Never before have we seen this.

sections.title: Common High-Level Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Confusion between Gerund and Participle. 2. Misidentifying the function of an Infinitive. 3. Forgetting the auxiliary verb during inversion. 4. Making decisions based only on the word's appearance rather than its syntax in functional grammar.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In functional grammar, a word's role is paramount. V1+ing can be either a Gerund or a Participle — always check its role. An Infinitive can function as a Noun, Adjective, or Adverb. Inversion is mandatory when a sentence starts with a negative adverb.

tricks.title: Role Check Trick
tricks.explanation: Step 1: Try removing the word. Step 2: Replace it with a known Noun, Verb, or Modifier. Step 3: Whatever fits dictates the Part of Speech. Step 4: Confirm that the basic meaning structure holds.
tricks.example: He ran fast. fast = How? → Adverb.

tricks.title: Gerund Identification Trick
tricks.explanation: Step 1: Identify V1+ing. Step 2: Is it the Subject or Object? Step 3: Replace it with 'it'. Step 4: If the sentence still makes sense, it's a Gerund.
tricks.example: Reading is fun. It is fun. → Reading = Gerund.

tricks.title: Participle Identification Trick
tricks.explanation: Step 1: Look for V1+ing. Step 2: Is it describing a Noun? Step 3: If yes, it is a Participle. Step 4: It functions like an Adjective.
tricks.example: The crying baby is hungry. crying = Participle.

tricks.title: Infinitive Function Trick
tricks.explanation: Step 1: Identify to + V1. Step 2: Is it showing a reason? → Adverb. Step 3: Is it qualifying a noun? → Adjective. Step 4: Is it a Subject/Object? → Noun.

tricks.title: Inversion Alert Trick
tricks.explanation: Step 1: Look for Never/Hardly at the start of the sentence. Step 2: Immediately bring the auxiliary forward. Step 3: Structure: Adverb + Auxiliary + Subject + Verb. Step 4: Double-check the tense.
tricks.example: Never have I seen such beauty.

tricks.title: Hardly/No sooner Pair Trick
tricks.explanation: Step 1: Pair 'Hardly' with 'when'. Step 2: Pair 'No sooner' with 'than'. Step 3: Use the past perfect tense generally. Step 4: Apply inversion.
tricks.example: No sooner had he arrived than it rained.

tricks.title: Multiple Role Word Trick
tricks.explanation: Step 1: Observe the same word in different sentences. Step 2: Identify its distinct role each time. Step 3: Determine the meaning from context. Step 4: Do not rely solely on the word's form.
tricks.example: They fast daily. (Verb) He observed a fast. (Noun)

tricks.title: Syntax First Trick
tricks.explanation: Step 1: Read the entire clause. Step 2: Identify the Subject-Verb-Object. Step 3: Check the position of the Modifier. Step 4: Determine the Part of Speech based on this structure.
tricks.example: He is a fast driver. fast → describes the driver → Adjective.
